title: Impression, Sunrise
credit: art database / Musée Marmottan Monet photograph on Wikimedia Commons
caption_long: Paint a harbor at first light: a low orange sun dissolving into lavender fog, water broken into loose horizontal strokes, dark boat silhouettes barely drawn. Let the air stay wet and unfinished, more weather than architecture. Thin oil, broken color, a quiet industrial haze turning gold. Keep it airy and just-waking, the scene felt rather than counted.
caption_short: a fogged harbor and orange sun dissolving into broken water.

title: Woman with a Parasol — Madame Monet and Her Son
credit: National Gallery of Art via Google Cultural Institute
caption_long: Paint a woman on a windy hill, white dress and green parasol against a huge pale sky. Grass streaks upward in green and gold; a small boy almost disappears into the meadow. Look up from below so the figure is backlit, veil and ribbons fluttering. Broken plein-air strokes, bright and breathable, a summer afternoon that will not sit still.
caption_short: a windblown woman with a green parasol on a bright hill.

title: Poppy Field
caption_long: Paint a sloping meadow of red poppies under a high, thin-cloud sky. Two small walkers drift through the flowers; a line of trees and a pale house sit far back. Scatter the reds like loose embroidery over green and gold grass. Soft wind, open country, broken color so the field flickers rather than holds still.
caption_short: a sloping poppy meadow under a thin-cloud summer sky.

title: The Artist's Garden at Giverny
caption_long: Paint a garden path sinking into iris and rose, cool violets and warm pinks crowding a pale walk. Tall stems close in; the air feels pollen-thick and green-shadowed. Use flickering oil dabs so flowers become light before they become petals. Intimate, overgrown, and luminous, a private garden at the hour when color is loudest.
caption_short: a crowded Giverny path lost in iris, rose, and green light.

title: Water Lilies
caption_long: Paint a pond surface with no horizon: drifting lily pads, pale blooms, and sky reflected as lavender, rose, and cloud-white. Let water and air trade places. Soft oil veils, almost no drawing, the surface breathing. Quiet, floating, and close, as if leaning over the water until the world becomes only color and ripple.
caption_short: a horizonless pond of lilies and reflected sky.

title: Girl in the Garden
caption_long: Paint a young woman seated in garden shade, white dress catching broken sun through leaves. Soft greens close around her; the face stays quiet and unposed. Pastel-like oil, airy and intimate, more afternoon than portrait. Let the light dapple rather than model, so the garden feels cooler than the dress.
caption_short: a quiet girl in a white dress, dappled by garden shade.

title: The Garden of the Tuileries on a Spring Morning
credit: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Douglas Dillon, 1992
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint the Tuileries from a high window on a spring morning: pale gravel paths, tiny walkers, new-green trees, a wide milky sky. Soft city haze, almost no hard edges. Flickering dabs of pink, cream, and leaf-green so the park breathes. Light, open, and civic, a Paris garden just waking.
caption_short: a high spring view over pale Tuileries paths and new leaves.

title: The Boulevard Montmartre on a Winter Morning
credit: Gift of Katrin S. Vietor, in loving memory of Ernest G. Vietor, 1960
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a Paris boulevard in winter morning fog: wet stone, carriages, and a pale lemon sky catching on shopfronts. Trees are bare gray veils; people are quick dark notes. Broken impressionist strokes, cool and pearly, city air more than architecture. Keep it light despite the season, a street dissolving into weather.
caption_short: a fogged winter boulevard catching pale lemon morning light.

provenance.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
provenance.repository: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY

title: Sahurs Meadows in Morning Sun
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint wide riverside meadows in early sun: a pale path, a few haystacks, water glinting at the edge, a sky of thin blue and white. Soft poplars, almost no shadow. High-key oil, breezy and open, the grass flickering gold-green. A quiet morning that feels washed and newly made.
caption_short: sunlit riverside meadows under a thin blue morning sky.

provenance.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
provenance.repository: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY

title: The Bridge at Villeneuve-la-Garenne
credit: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Henry Ittleson Jr., 1964
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a white iron bridge spanning bright river water, flags and little boats, a village of pale houses under a clear sky. The river holds broken blues and the bridge throws cool shade. Fresh plein-air oil, sparkling and clean, summer on the Seine without heaviness.
caption_short: a white river bridge and bright boats on sparkling Seine water.

provenance.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
provenance.repository: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY

title: Allée of Chestnut Trees
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a receding allée of chestnut trees, a pale road between trunks, figures walking into green shade. Dappled sun on the track; foliage is flickering leaf-light more than leaves. Soft impressionist oil, rural and airy, the path pulling you into cool summer depth.
caption_short: a pale country road receding through flickering chestnut shade.

provenance.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access
provenance.repository: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, NY

title: Nini in the Garden (Nini Lopez)
credit: The Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection, Gift of Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg, 2002, Bequest of Walter H. Annenberg, 2002
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a young woman seated in garden shade, a pale dress among loose green and rose. Sun breaks the foliage in warm flecks; the face stays soft. Feathery impressionist oil, intimate and outdoor, more light on cloth than likeness. A private afternoon that feels half-dreamed.
caption_short: a young woman in a pale dress, seated in flecked garden light.

title: By the Seashore
credit: H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a woman in a flowered hat against a high, breezy sea, cliffs dissolving into pale blue. Her dress is cream and rose; the water behind her sparkles in broken strokes. Open air, salt light, impressionist and pretty without heaviness. Keep the horizon soft so she seems held by weather.
caption_short: a flower-hatted woman against a breezy, pale blue sea.

title: Chrysanthemums in the Garden at Petit-Gennevilliers
credit: Gift of the Honorable John C. Whitehead, 2014
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a late-garden bed of chrysanthemums: rust, cream, and yellow blooms crowding a gravel path, a pale house half-hidden. Cool autumn light, leaves just turning. Impressionist oil that stays close to the flowers, airy and domestic, more garden weather than still life.
caption_short: autumn chrysanthemums crowding a pale garden path.

title: At the Seaside
credit: Bequest of Miss Adelaide Milton de Groot (1876-1967), 1967
license_note: The Met Open Access API marks this object as public domain.
caption_long: Paint a pale beach under a huge summer sky: women and children in white, a few umbrellas, the sea a thin turquoise band. Sand is cream and lilac; figures are quick notes. American impressionist oil, open and breezy, salt air and idle afternoon. Keep it high-key so the day feels endless.
caption_short: a pale beach of white dresses under a huge summer sky.
